Methods for simultaneously discovering exceptions and identifying incorrect data in large
databases are referred to as anomaly detection methods. In Chi Square Tests for Anomaly
Detection in XML Documents Using Negative Association Rules, by Permalatta and etc.
found at ccsenet.org/journal/index.php/cis/article/view/1852, detected the detection anoma-
lies in nested XML documents by independence between data.
This naturally leads the investigator to the application of the Chi Square test.
n What is a negative association rule?

Why is the Chi-Square statistic so well known? It is the most commonly used test to deter-
mine if an observed dataset satisfies a specified distribution. The test is general and can be
used for any distribution. It can be used for testing random numbers, as well as for testing
random-variate generators Additionally, as in the header file, the Chi-Square Statistic can be
used to determine whether or not two variates are related.
More importantly is that the chi-square distribution can be used to make inferences about a
single population variance. Secondly, it is related to the F distribution, used to study two pop-
ulation variances. The F distribution is proportional to the ratio of two chi-square statistics.

21.1 Introduction
Often a manager will suspect that orders come from several mutually exclusive categories,
each with a specified percentage. The manager might attempt to obtain a sample of size n
and determine the breakdown of the sample into the various categories. Using these sample
percentages, the manager could then test the original hunch concerning the actual categori-
cal percentages at a specified confidence level. In this chapter, we will study how to perform
a hypothesis test using the chi-square distribution to solve such a problem, based upon a
multinomial distribution.

Calculations of probabilities for the multinomial distribution are tedious when n is large, but

In a dataset, a multinomial variable is one whose values, not necessarily numerical, can be
classified into three or more categories; that is, whose values are nominal. If we take a sample
from a population of multinomial data (for example, ask a random group of voters to name
their first choice for president), the probabilities with which various numbers of responses
from the categories occur in the sample are described by the multinomial distribution, while
the probabilities of various numbers of elements of type i occurring in the sample are given
by the binomial distribution b (n, p

21.3 Exercises
Computational and i nterpretational e xercises
1. A large population of objects is one-half type As, one-third type Bs, and one-sixth
type Cs. If a sample of 10 objects is randomly selected, what is the probability that it
contains 6 type As, 3 type Bs, and 1 type C?
2. A machine is designed to mix nuts in the following proportions: 20% peanuts, 25%
cashews, 15% pecans, 30% walnuts, and 10% acorns. In a bag of 200 nuts, there are
35 peanuts, 55 cashews, 25 pecans, 60 walnuts, and 25 acorns. At the 1% significance
level, should it be concluded that the machine is not mixing nuts in the specified
proportions?
3. The manager of a mail-order firm believes that 10% of the orders come from the
West, 20% from the South, 40% from the East, 20% from the Midwest, and 10%
from foreign countries. A sample of 125 orders has these destinations:
West 20
South 33
East 14
Midwest 48
Foreign 10
Total 125
At the 5% significance level, is the manager correct about the proportions?
4. In your opinion, what proportions of your class would agree with each of the
responses to this question:
Check the one statement with which you most agree.
___________ On the whole, wars do the world some good.
___________ Peace and war are both essential to progress.
___________ War is hardly ever necessary in the modern world.
___________ There is no conceivable justification for war.
Administer the question to the class, and test your proposed proportions at the 5%
significance level.

above 10% are each one-fourth. Use the significance level of 5%.
